turns.prompt_text: Where can I buy different wood for a different wood crafts?
turns.response_html:
For a variety of wood crafts, you can find different types of lumber, live-edge slabs, and specialty hobby parts through several local and online suppliers.

Local Suppliers in Ames and Central Iowa

Since you are in the Ames area, you have access to local sawmills that offer unique, native Iowa woods:

  • Iowa Home Crafters: Located right in Ames, they mill and kiln-dry native Iowa woods like walnut, oak, maple, and cherry. They offer wood slabs for sale to the general public, including live-edge pieces that are popular for furniture and artistic crafts.
  • Twister Hill Hardwoods: Based in Central Iowa, this family-owned sawmill specializes in Midwest hardwoods and live-edge slabs. They offer both rough-sawn and milled lumber, including species like Black Walnut.
  • Munn Lumber: A local building partner in Ames (located on Airport Rd) that carries hardwoods and cedar in addition to standard construction lumber. They are a good option if you need specific dimensional hardwoods for project builds.
  • Lowe’s of Ames: For more common lumber, craft boards (like poplar or balsa), and basic woodworking tools, the Lowe's on Airport Rd carries a standard selection of hobbyist wood.

Online Specialty & Craft Wood Suppliers

If you are looking for specific pre-cut parts or exotic species not found locally, these online resources are highly rated:

  • Craftparts.com: A premium supplier for wooden hobby parts. This is a great source if your crafts involve specific shapes like dowels, toy wheels, beads, peg dolls, or wooden cubes.
  • American Woodcrafters Supply: They offer a "one-stop shop" experience for wood crafting needs, ranging from axle pegs and spindles to shaker pegs and furniture plugs.
  • Blick Art Materials: Excellent for smaller-scale craft wood, such as basswood strips, balsa wood for modeling, and various craft sticks.

Identifying the Right Wood for Your Craft

Depending on the specific "different wood craft" you are pursuing, consider these categories:

  • For Carving/Whittling: Look for Basswood, which is soft and has a very fine grain, making it the gold standard for beginners and pros alike.
  • For Furniture or Heirlooms: Walnut, Cherry, or Maple from local mills like Iowa Home Crafters will provide the best durability and aesthetic.
  • For Laser Cutting/Engraving: Thin plywood (3mm or 1/8") or "Project Boards" found at hobby shops or Munn Lumber are ideal.
  • For Small Models: Balsa or Paulownia wood is extremely lightweight and easy to cut with a hobby knife.
